current_price_source: Yahoo Finance chart API, ANN.AX regularMarketPrice
horizon_rationale: 10 years: base-case margins are essentially mature by Y4 but the bear case needs the FY27-28 destock/tariff drawdown and recovery to play out before capitalization, and the entry-price and required-return machinery in this folder assume N=10.
wacc_rationale: Built from the flows' currency (USD): risk-free 4.2% (UST 10y, Sep-2026), ERP 5.0%, beta 1.0 (global industrial/healthcare consumables) -> cost of equity 9.2%; pre-tax cost of debt 5.2% (FY26 interest on borrowings $35.3m / ~$678m average gross debt) -> 3.95% after tax at 24%; market weights E 87% / D 13% (market cap US$4.28bn vs $657m gross debt) -> WACC 8.5%, rounded. Same rate in all three scenarios: cyclicality, tariff and destocking risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).

inputs.share_count_basis: 139.4m ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY26 five-year summary, after the $118.4m FY26 on-market buyback) plus 1.0m potential ordinary shares from the FY26 diluted-EPS note = 140.4m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, and the on-market buyback plus treasury purchases are the cash mechanism that keeps it flat (charging both would double-count). The 143.8m in Metrics.csv is the FY26 weighted-average diluted denominator, not the year-end count.
inputs.lease_treatment: B: leases as operating cost. Lease principal ($23.4m, financing) and lease interest ($5.4m, financing) are deducted from the flows as lease_cost_pct 1.35% of revenue; lease liabilities ($99.4m) are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (79.7 - ~23.4 = ~56.3, 2.6% of revenue; the ROU depreciation charge is not broken out in the extracted leases note, so it is taken as equal to the principal repayment).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated (NCI profit share $1.0m in FY26 is inside adjusted EBIT); the $30.9m NCI book value is deducted once in the equity bridge. Calibration: FY26 modelled NOPAT ~ (321.9 - 5.4 lease interest) x 0.76 = $240m vs reported attributable NPAT $208.6m after $35.3m interest on borrowings x 0.76 = $26.8m -> $213m, a $27m gap that is the significant items ($1.4m), the $25.2m PPE write-down inside adjusted EBIT, and the cash/P&L tax difference.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest received $4.4m (P&L interest income $4.3m) stripped from the owner-FCF base because the $249.5m cash it earns is netted in the bridge (matching-asset rule). The company is net-debt so the adjustment is immaterial (1.5% of owner FCF). Interest PAID on borrowings sits in financing activities for Ansell, so reported OCF is already pre-interest-expense and the historical owner-FCF series is unlevered without further adjustment.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 Annual Report note 6(b) OCF reconciliation 'Share-based payments expense 11.6' (FY25 9.1); no separate equity-award tax withholding line is disclosed -- Ansell buys treasury shares on-market to settle awards ($17.4m FY26), which is the buyback mechanism, not an additional cost.
inputs.buyback_note: FY26 on-market buyback $118.4m (program announced Aug-2025) plus $17.4m treasury purchases for employee plans; issued shares fell 145.2m -> 139.4m. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (flat count, SBC expensed); the $118.4m is reported so the reader can see the flat count IS being funded. Metrics.csv ShareRepurchases FY2021-FY2024 reads 0; the filings show $14.3m/$14.6m/$8.0m/$30.0m of employee-plan treasury purchases in those years, which the parser classed as non-buyback.
inputs.normalized_owner_fcf_fy26_note: FY26 printed owner FCF $294.8m (13.8% of sales) is a cyclical high: capex $49.0m was 2.3% of sales against a FY22-25 range of 3.5-4.1%, and OCF carried a net working-capital/tax-timing inflow of ~$18m (inventory -$82.6m release after the FY25 KBU build). Rebuilding FY26 from components at 3.2% capex, 20% WC absorption on growth and a 24% cash tax rate gives ~$215-225m (~10% of sales), which is the level the Y1 projection carries. The FY22-26 average owner-FCF margin is 8.8%.
inputs.guidance_vintage: FY26 Annual Report (year ended 30-Jun-2026, published Aug-2026): FY27 outlook is qualitative only -- constant-currency sales growth from higher volumes and FY26 pricing actions, earnings growth from commercial excellence and productivity; no EPS range given in the report.
inputs.fx_rate_direction: AUD -> USD multiplier (AUDUSD=X): takes the ASX price in AUD to the USD of the financials; per-share USD values are divided by it to reach AUD. Used by scripts/sanity_check.py.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in USD ('The Financial Report is presented in United States dollars', every filing FY2015-FY2026); ASX quote in AUD. All per-share values computed in USD then converted at AUDUSD 0.7132 (Yahoo AUDUSD=X, 2026-09-21T11:08:08Z; 52wk 0.6422-0.7277, so the AUD is near a 12-month high -- a 5% AUD retreat would LIFT every AUD value here ~5%). No liquid dual listing exists for a parity check (ANNSF OTC is untraded); direction verified by magnitude: base IV US$22.99 -> A$32.24, i.e. AUD figures are 1.402x USD figures, consistent with 1/AUDUSD. Unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv / entry_price are AUD (quote currency) so they compare to current_price; _usd twins carry the reporting-currency basis.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component-built, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials' -> references/owner-fcf.md incl. section 7). Ansell is a global manufacturer of hand and body protection (Healthcare 56% / Industrial 44% of FY26 sales), a plain operating company with a normal cash-flow statement, so no non-FCF model applies. Cyclical adaptations applied: (a) WACC in USD, the flows' currency, with AUD as quote currency and an FX bridge; (b) lease treatment B, leases in flows and out of net debt; (c) NCI deducted once in the bridge; (d) interest received stripped, cash in the bridge; (e) SBC kept explicit at 0.55% of revenue (near-SBC-zero); (f) risk charged once -- single WACC, cyclicality in the scenario flows and a 20% bear weight. Mid-cycle: the Y1 owner-FCF margin (~9-10%) is built from components, NOT carried forward from FY26's 13.8%, because FY26 combined a decade-low capex ratio with an inventory release after the FY23-24 destock and FY25 KBU inventory build. Terminal cap 15x owner FCF (cyclical industrial), which binds in every scenario against Gordon at 8.5% WACC.

historical_growth.fcf_basis: owner FCF = OCF - capex - SBC - interest received - lease principal - lease interest (pre-FY2020 leases were already in OCF under AASB 117)
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case Y1-Y5 average revenue growth (5.0/4.5/4.0/3.5/3.0). Equity CAGR rejected: FY2024 carries a $400m equity raise for KBU, and FY2018 carries the $600m Sexual Wellness divestment gain; EPS CAGRs run peak-to-trough across the COVID glove cycle.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 5.3% vs revenue 5yr 1.1% and EPS 5yr -5.4%: divergence >30% on both. Revenue FY2021 base is the COVID peak (exam-glove demand), FY2024 is the destocking trough, FY2025-26 include ~$400m acquired KBU revenue. No single historical CAGR describes the underlying business; the base-case path is anchored on FY26 organic constant-currency growth (5.0%) and the qualitative FY27 outlook (volume + pricing growth, no number given).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (46%/50%) are trough-to-peak artefacts: FY2021 owner FCF of $38.5m sits under a $30.1m CEO-succession SBC charge and a COVID inventory build; FY2023 under the destock; FY2026 is a working-capital release year ($82.6m inventory decrease) with capex at a decade-low 2.3% of sales. The five-year average owner-FCF margin FY2022-26 is 8.8%; the component-built normalized FY26 margin is ~10%, which is what the Y1 projection carries, not the 13.8% printed.

scenario_narratives.base: FY27 delivers the qualitative guide -- constant-currency sales growth from volume plus FY26 pricing actions -- at ~5% (FY26 organic CC was 5.0%, FY25 7.7%), fading to 3% as the KBU cross-sell and US channel gains mature and to 2.5% by Y9-10. Adjusted EBITDA margin drifts from 18.8% to 19.2% (Adj EBIT ~15.0% -> ~15.4%) as APIP footprint savings and the India surgical greenfield offset tariff and labour inflation; that is the top of Ansell's FY19-FY26 EBIT-margin range ex the COVID year, so no further re-rating is assumed. Capex normalises from FY26's 2.3% trough to 3.2% of sales; working capital absorbs 20c per dollar of growth (net WC is 24% of sales); cash tax 24% (adjusted ETR 24.1%). Count flat at 140.4m, funded by the ongoing buyback.
scenario_narratives.bull: US share gains and KBU cross-selling into scientific, cleanroom (FY26 +10%) and life-sciences verticals hold growth at 8% in FY27 fading to 3.5%; tariff pass-through sticks and mix shifts toward differentiated Industrial/surgical product, taking Adj EBITDA margin to 21% (Adj EBIT ~17%, a level Ansell has only touched in FY21's COVID year). Capex 3.0%, cash tax 23.5%, terminal growth 3%. This case needs both above-market growth and record margins simultaneously, which is why its weight is below the house default.
scenario_narratives.bear: A second destocking cycle or US recession repeats the FY23-24 pattern (revenue fell 20% from the FY21 peak to the FY24 trough, Adj EBIT margin 12%): FY27 revenue -2%, flat FY28, then 2-2.5% growth. US tariffs on Malaysian, Thai and Sri Lankan glove production are not fully passed through, and Chinese exam-glove price competition compresses Healthcare margins, so Adj EBITDA margin resets to 16.5% (Adj EBIT ~12.5-13%, the FY22-24 average) and stays there. Capex 3.4%, cash tax 25%, terminal growth 2%. The balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA ~1.0x) carries this case without a solvency question, which is why the bear weight is 20% and not higher.

base.equity_bridge_usd_m: EV - net debt 407.7 (ex-lease; leases charged in flows) - NCI 30.9

bull.equity_bridge_usd_m: EV - net debt 407.7 (ex-lease; leases charged in flows) - NCI 30.9

bear.equity_bridge_usd_m: EV - net debt 407.7 (ex-lease; leases charged in flows) - NCI 30.9

entry_price.method_note: Price at which buying today, collecting the projected owner FCF for 10 years and exiting at a terminal value built AT THE HURDLE RATE (min(Gordon@15%, 15x FCF_10)) returns a 15% IRR, less net debt and NCI, per fully diluted share. Computed per scenario and probability-weighted. Self-consistency check passed: the IRR implied by the base entry price with TV rebuilt at that IRR is 15.0%.
entry_price.note: Entry prices sit at 44% of intrinsic value, the expected gap when demanding 15% from an asset discounted at 8.5%. The bear-case entry price is a third of the current price: a 15% return from here needs the bull case.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_10)). The 8.5% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price. Today's A$42.71 sits between the 8.5% row and the 7.5% sensitivity row: the market is pricing roughly a 7% USD return on the base path.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth; base drivers; TV = max(0, min(Gordon, 15x FCF_10)) rebuilt per cell. The 15x cap binds at every WACC <= 9.5% for g >= 2%, which is why the grid is flat across g in the upper rows -- the valuation is a multiple call, not a terminal-growth call.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 20% bear / 50% base / 30% bull against the house 15/50/35. Bear raised because the FY23-24 destock shows a 20% revenue drawdown and 300bp EBIT-margin compression is a live pattern for this business, and US tariffs on Southeast-Asian glove production are a current, unresolved axis; not higher because gearing is ~1.0x EBITDA and no going-concern or covenant question exists. Bull lowered because it requires above-market growth AND record margins at the same time.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band is only A$2.23 wide because SBC is 0.55% of revenue; the price sits 432% along it, i.e. well above the street ceiling. SBC treatment is not what separates price from value here -- the exit multiple and margin assumptions are.

implied_multiples_at_price.note: Lease-consistent: ex-lease EV over pre-IFRS16 EBITDA, or lease-inclusive EV over post-IFRS16 EBITDA.

valuation_philosophy.basis: house owner-FCF, SBC expensed, leases as operating cost, NCI deducted
valuation_philosophy.mid_cycle: Y1 owner-FCF margin rebuilt from components at normal capex and working-capital absorption rather than FY26's release-year print
valuation_philosophy.terminal: 15x owner FCF cap for a cyclical industrial; binds in all scenarios
valuation_philosophy.risk: charged once, in the flows and weights; single 8.5% USD WACC

data_quality_notes: Metrics.csv shares_outstanding 143.8 (FY2026) is the weighted-average diluted denominator; the year-end count is 139.4m basic / 140.4m diluted and the model uses the latter.
Metrics.csv ShareRepurchases FY2021-FY2024 = 0 reflects only on-market buyback programs; employee-plan treasury purchases ($14.3m/$14.6m/$8.0m/$30.0m) exist in the filings.
FY2018 owner FCF includes the part-year Sexual Wellness business (sold FY18 for ~$600m); FY2018 net income $486.2m is the disposal gain.
FY2024 shareholders' equity includes the $400m Jun-2024 equity raise for the KBU acquisition; FY2024 cash $912.3m and debt $766.3m were pre-funding for the Jul-2024 completion.
ROU depreciation is not broken out in the extracted FY26 leases note; taken as equal to lease principal repaid ($23.4m) for the D&A ex-ROU estimate.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
